criteria.description: Tests whether the product shell generalizes beyond the thermal-control domain.
Supports a bounded, dependency-free model with clear inputs, outputs, assumptions, and failure conditions.
Can be explored entirely with synthetic or canonical data without physical intervention or live-system traffic.
Has a reviewed system dossier, failure pattern, investigation, and design challenge.
Contains a strong mechanism-level distinction between normal operation, degradation, and amplified failure.
Supports meaningful redesign choices with visible trade-offs rather than one correct component swap.
Naturally supports accessibility, low-bandwidth, privacy, and degraded-mode reasoning.
Higher scores mean the route can begin without speculative Atlas expansion.

candidates.title: Solar, Storage, Protection, and Resilient Service
candidates.judgment: Strong system depth and redesign value, but protection, islanding, batteries, and electrical safety make it a poor first test of the reusable learner shell.

candidates.title: Water Treatment, Distribution, Measurement, and Storage
candidates.judgment: Excellent cross-domain systems reasoning, but public-health boundaries and the separation between treatment behavior and potable-safety claims add avoidable first-expansion complexity.

candidates.title: Distributed Web Service, Queueing, and Recovery
candidates.judgment: Best first generalization test: maximally different from refrigerator, fully synthetic and offline, quantitatively bounded, diagnostically strong, and rich in performance, accessibility, privacy, reliability, and governance trade-offs.

decision.rationale: Distributed information has the highest weighted score and tests the greatest architectural distance from the refrigerator route without introducing physical, electrical, or public-health execution risk. Its queueing model supports prediction-before-model interaction, its retry-storm failure supports mechanism-level diagnosis, and its school information service challenge supports redesign across performance, accessibility, privacy, resilience, and operational complexity.
next_deliverables: implement a route-driven model adapter interface
remove thermal labels and controls from the generic learner shell
add a buildable distributed-information route configuration
preserve refrigerator output and deterministic behavior
run both routes through focused JavaScript and Python regression coverage
deferred: Atlas expansion without a concrete exact-revision evidence gap
accounts, analytics, cloud storage, or public deployment

may_claim: authorization to refactor the learner shell for multiple model adapters
